page_copy._geo keys a program on the TensorAccessor compile-time args AND the shape of a sharded tensor, so a program built for one slab geometry is never reused for another (served slabs of other batch counts)
HOST_GLUE's load-time snapshot would freeze POS_DYNAMIC: hooks.batch_call_apply refreshes that one switch in a held model's snapshot (call-time switch)
only POS_DYNAMIC is written into settings.snap (batch_call_apply, test_no_rebuild's on/off check), never a full refresh()
decode truncates a fresh slot's window at its first chunk, so test_no_rebuild draws every request at a new AgentX position in a new slot and compile can warm a pulled-back chunk
page copies / IdsReorder keep per-core runtime args to a few cores (4 / 1) so a dispatch's per-chip args stay small

overseer.evidence: every listed site is a runtime value under POS_DYNAMIC=on: rope.py/compressor.py row slices -> page_copy with sp_stride; served.DeviceScalars._pick and CacheSlab.slice_rows -> page copies (slot x layers + row a value); history_gather _pack/_tail fixed row counts + page copies; attention.srv_row page copy; compressor._write_from replay rotation = 2 page copies; snapshot_send pattern as values (batching PB.7C); unpack_fp8_rows whole_grid; partial masks were already runtime (ttnn.lt scalar: no build in the partial / acks-only draws); ids reordered on the device (IdsReorder, no _host_emb_ids upload); adapter.compile warms the finite set. test_no_rebuild: builds 0, prepares 0, ids uploads 0, on vs off 0.0; fresh walls 0 builds, fresh ~= warm

no weight or tensor is padded for a kernel limit; but to keep ONE shape (rule 20) the history tail always gathers 2 hs rows (on a chunk-aligned start hs rows of it were already prefetched: re-sent, same bytes) and the whole-history pack runs in PACK_BUCKET pieces whose last piece may overlap the previous one. Measured: fresh walls steady 61.4k tok/s vs MB.1's repeated 63.4k (warm repeated 61.2k): within ~3 ms a chunk. Removing it needs slice_write / the tail gather to take the row count as a runtime value (a fork change); proposed as a follow-up, not done in this step
